997.name: Hints1
997.text:
2,10,12,16,18,26,30,33,30,33,35,37,39,42,44,47,49,50,52,54,55,55,57,67
Click here to build a sod house. 
On the Great Plains,  there were no forests, 
so it was difficult and expensive  to build 
wooden houses. People cut the layer of grass 
and soil that forms the surface of the ground,
called sod,  into strips. After the strips of sod 
dried in the sun,  they were used as bricks to
build houses. You need a house to survive
the cold Kansas winters.

Click here to build a barn and a wooden fence 
around the barn. The barn has stalls where
the animals live and a dry place  to store their food.
The animals need a barn to survive
the cold Kansas winters.

Click here to dig a well and build a windmill. 
There were few water sources on the Great Plains. 
Many people dug wells to find water that 
was deep underground.  They used windmills to 
pump water out of the ground. 
Wind power turns propellers on a windmill.
When the propellers turn, a pump pushes the water
up to a small pool on the land surface.  You need 
water to keep your family and your animals alive.

Click here to build a wooden fence around the field. 

Click here to build a barbed-wire fence around the field.
A barbed-wire fence is better than a wooden fence
for keeping  animals out of the field.
Its sharp pieces hurt animals that touch the fence.

Click here to see which family members can help you.
Different people are available at different times. 
Decide how many family members you want to help you.

Click here to see which neighbors can help you. 
Neighbors are usually happy to help you when 
you are ready to help them. Decide how many neighbors 
you want to help you.

Click here to hire workers to help you. 
Workers are paid by the day. 
Decide how many workers you want to hire. 
When their work is done, it is time to pay them.

This shows how many days it will take to finish
the job with the number of helpers you chose.

This shows how much you will pay for the material
you need and the workers you hired for this building job.

Click here if you are sure you want to build.

Click here if you decide not to build.

998.name: Hints
998.text:
2,4,6,8,10,13,10,13,15,19,20,24,26,28,30,31,33,34,35,36,38,39,41,44,46,47,48,49
The general store, the bank and the grain elevator are
in the town. You can learn about new business
opportunities there.

In your house, you can read the newspapers, 
hide your savings,
and keep a record of your life.

You can earn money by working in the fields. 
Try to make good decisions about plowing your fields, 
planting your seeds,
and harvesting and selling your crops.

The calendar shows the passage of time.
When the button on top of the calendar is green, 
the calendar is running. Click on it to stop time from passing.
When the button on top of the calendar is red,
the calendar is stopped. Click on it to start running it again.
When you hear the trumpet, choose a trivia card.
If you answer  the question on the card correctly, 
you will win some money.  Tip: You can find answers
to the trivia questions by reading the  newspapers
and listening to the conversations in town.

Click here to see what you have achieved 
so far in the game. You can see how much money you have,
what you own, and how close you are to your goal.

When the red flag on the mailbox is raised, the mailman
has delivered a letter for you. Click on the mailbox to read the letter.

Click here to start over, save your work, 
see the introduction, or exit.
Click here to visit with some of your neighbors.
They always have something interesting to say.

Each spring you can go to the livestock fair
to buy and sell animals.

Click on the hammer when you want to build things.
To survive, you need a house, a barn, and a well with
a windmill, so build them as soon as you can. You can
also build a fence to protect your crops from animals.

This is how much money you have in cash.

This is how much money you have in your savings box.

 I've heard about a new kind of fence, but it's not in the general store's catalog yet.

1038.name: Rep
1038.text:
That was some tornado, neighbor.
If I were you, I'd fix everything that was
damaged as soon as possible. 
In another month or two, it will be too cold
to work outside. Anyway, your animals won't 
make it through the winter without a barn.

1039.name: CantBuild
1039.text:
It's too cold to build anything right now.
You need to wait until early spring.

1040.name: NoBuild
1040.text:
Neighbor, please let me and some
other folks help you build a barn.
Your animals need some shade and
protection from the rain. 
You should also dig a well soon.
By July, the creek will be almost dry.

1041.name: NoWM
1041.text: It's very difficult to carry water in pails all the way from the creek. Now the creek is nearly dry. Our neighbors say that if we buy a windmill, they’ll help us build it and dig a well.

1042.name: OnlyBuild
1042.text: I'm tired of carrying water from the creek far away. Can we please build the windmill you've bought?

1043.name: NoBarn

1045.name: AnimD
1045.text: The cold weather killed all your animals. Since you don't have a dairy cow, it will cost $10 dollars a month to buy milk from a neighbor.

1046.name: NoHouse

1047.name: YesHouse

My baby's name is:

1048.text: Hello, neighbor. Looks like the tornado left your farm in pretty bad shape! If you need help repairing  things, just ask  for it!

1049.name: Da1
1049.text: Ouch! My feet hurt. My shoes are  too small. Will you please buy me a new pair? They cost five dollars.

1051.name: Da3

I have good news! I've been accepted
 to college. If you lend me $480.00 a year
 to help pay for school,
I can go. Will you help me?

1052.name: Da4
1052.text:
I''ve been offered another chance to teach scool in town, and I'd really like to take it. I'll miss everyone, but I'm looking forward to living in a big city. My train leaves in a few days. I'll write from Boston to tell you
how I'm doing.

1053.name: DAW1
1053.text: Now that I'm older, I can help you in the fields when you're busy. I may miss some school, but you'll finish the work faster and save money.

1054.name: DAW3
1054.text: Now that I've finished school, I can work full-time in the fields. I can work as hard as any worker you could hire.

1055.name: DAW5
1055.text: A very nice family in town wants me to live with them and work as a mother's helper. Now that I'm grown up, I want a chance to be on my own. May I take the job?

1056.name: DAW7

I'd really like to take it, but it would mean 
moving to town. Will you let me leave home
and take the job?

1058.name: Daw9
1058.text: I've been offered another chance to teach school in town, and I'd really like to take it. It would mean moving to town. Will you let me leave home and take the job?

1059.name: DMail
1059.text: Hello, neighbor. Starting this month, your mail will be delivered to your house.  Whenever there's a letter for you, the red flag on your mailbox will be raised. Your mail won't come to my store anymore, but I hope I'll still see you there often.

1060.name: Dat5
1060.text: I've applied to Oberlin College, in Ohio. Maybe someday I'll be able to teach college, as some women are starting to do. Soon I'll hear whether the college has accepted me.

1061.name: MyHelp

1069.name: Sop4

1077.name: Son3
1077.text: Ma, Pa, I've made up my mind. I'm going to California to seek my fortune. Please don't worry about me. I'll write you as soon as I get there.

1140.text:
TOWN OF LONGVIEW
                                             BUFFALO COUNTY, KANSAS

 The people of Longview want to know where you stand.
 Click on the issues you support :

        America should get involved in the war in Europe.
       
        All women in America should be allowed to vote.
     
        Kansas should remain a "dry" state.    
         
        The federal government should own and operate the railroads.
       
        Ranchers should be put in jail for grazing their cattle on farmland. 
       
        Citizens under 18 years of age should be allowed to carry pistols in town.

1167.name: DLL
1167.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Our greatest fear has come true. Our sons are going off to fight 
in the war.  I hope they meet their Uncle Igorkggfgjgjfgfgf over there,
so he an look out for them. 
Billy and Davey are only 19 and 21 years old.

Please let me know if you hear any news from Igorkggfgjgjfgfgf.
I've heard that he's going to a place in France where the most
important battles are being fought.

John sends his love.

Your loving daughter,

1169.name: DL1
1169.text:
Dear Neighbor, 

We are asking everyone in this district of Buffalo County to 
donate money for building a schoolhouse for our children. 

Thank you so much for your help.
 


Ed Ducatur
Superintendent

1170.name: DL8
1170.text:
Dear Neighbor,

We are asking everyone in this district of Buffalo County
to donate money for building a new church. 
We also want to buy a bell for the belfry. Will you help us?  

Thank you so much.

Faithfully yours,


Reverend Stowell

1171.name: DL9
1171.text:
Dear Neighbor,

We are asking everyone in this district of Buffalo County
to donate money for fixing up our schoolhouse. 
The building is old and needs many repairs.

Thank you so much for your help.


T. Chair
Superintendent

1172.name: DL10
1172.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

It's been a year since the beautiful wedding you made for us. 
We finally reached Detroit. Living in a city is a big change, and I                                             already miss everyone back home.  John is looking forward to                                                   starting his job at the mill.In the meantime, we're stretching our                                                    dollars as much as we can.
Would you be able to help us?
John says that we don't need more than $150. 
Can you spare it? We promise to pay you back.
Please give my love to everyone.

Your loving daughter,

1173.name: DL11
1173.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,
How are you? I'm writing from way up north on the Klondike River.
I'm in Canada, just a few miles shy of the border with Alaska.

They've found gold in these parts, and I aim to find some myself.
Since your family was always good to me, I thought I would let 
you in on the loot.
If you lend me $75, I can set up camp here and start gold hunting.
I promise to give you ten percent of all the gold I find.

What do you say, cousin? Will you take a chance?

Your cousin,

1174.name: DL16
1174.text:
Dear Neighbor,

We are asking everyone in this district of Buffalo County
to donate money for building an addition to our
schoolhouse. There is simply no room in the current 
building for all our students.

Thank you so much for your help.



T. Chair
Superintendent

1175.name: DL17
1175.text:
Dear Neighbor,

We are asking everyone in this district of Buffalo County
to donate money for the big Fourth of July celebration we are
planning this year.It will be an especially big celebration because         we are also celebrating the turn of the century. We want to show everyone how proud we are to be Americans.
Thank you so much for your help.

Yours sincerely,


Charles Cane
Mayor

1176.name: DL18
1176.text:
Dear Neighbor,

We are asking everyone in the town of Longview and
the surrounding area to donate money for repairing our roads.  
As we all know, Main Street is full of holes. Route 28,
which runs from north to south through Longview, is also in             terrible condition. Taxes alone will not cover the cost of these repairs. 

Thank you for doing your part.


Bill Dozer
Longview Town Improvement Committee

1177.name: DL19
1177.text:
Dear Cousin, 

I hope you are doing well on your homestead on the range.

We are still living in New York City and working at the same jobs.

We have another chance to start a business with some friends. 
Once again, are you interested in investing $500.00
in our business?
If you invest, you'll get five percent of the profits.

I hope that you will write me soon.

Yours,

1178.name: DL20
1178.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I am writing you from sunny California. I arrived two weeks ago, 
after many adventures along the way.

In a few months I'll be able to find work in the citrus groves.
In the meantime, it's hard to live. Could you please send 
$100.00 to tide me over until harvest time?

Your loving son,

1179.name: DL21
1179.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm sorry that it's taken so long for me to write. It took                                                                                                           me a long time to find a job. Before I found work, I ran                                                                                                      out of money and went into debt. Now I'm working
to pay off my debts, and I don't have a penny  to spare                                                                                                         at the end of the week.

I want to come back to the farm, where I belong, but I                                                                                                         need  your help. If you send me $200.00, I can pay off                                                                                                           my  debts and come home.

Your loving son,

1180.name: DL22
1180.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm sorry that it's taken so long for me to write. It took                                                                             me a long time to find a job. Before I found work, I ran                                                                            out of money and went into debt. Now I'm working
to pay off my debts, and I don't have a penny to spare 
at the end of the week.

I want to come back to the farm, where I belong, but 
I need your help. If you send me $200.00, I can pay off                                                                          my debts and come home.

Your loving son,

1181.name: DL24
1181.text:
Dear Neighbor,

We've all noticed something new in our town lately.
It seems that everyone is driving automobiles, 
especially the Model T Ford.  
For the past year, folks have been complaining that our roads 
should be paved. Instead of raising taxes to pay for the work, 
we are asking everyone in the town of Longview and
the nearby area to help as much as they can.  
I hope that you are willing to pitch in.



Bill Dozer
Longview Town Improvement Committee

1182.name: DL28
1182.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

It's been a long time since we've been in touch. I've been                                                                                         working my way east from the West Coast, buying and 
selling properties on the way. Now I'm nearby, in the town                                                                                              of  Wichita, Kansas. Not far from here, some folks have                                                                                               struck oil.  I'm buying up land in the neighborhood so that                                                                                              I can strike it rich too! I thought I'd give you the first shot at                                                                                        investing in the well we're digging.  It will only cost you $800.                                                                                       You will get  20 percent of our profit.  If we strike oil, we could                                                                                      make millions!  Are you willing to take a chance?

Yours Cousin George.

1209.name: ALM1
1209.text:
Dear 

We are pleased to tell you that you have been elected to
represent the Longview branch of the Farmers' Alliance.
We will be honored to see you at all our county meetings.

Congratulations!


J.W. Paton
President

1210.name: ALM2
1210.text:
Dear 

I am very pleased to tell you that you have been elected
to the Longview School Board. You are a well-respected 
member of our community, and we believe you will be a 
valuable addition to our board.

We look forward to seeing you at our meetings!

Yours sincerely,


Ed Ducatur
Superintendent

1211.name: ALM3
1211.text:
Dear 

Congratulations! You have been elected president of the
Longview School Board. 
Everyone appreciates your fine work in the community.

Best wishes, 


Ed Ducatur
Superintendent

1212.name: ALM4
1212.text:
Dear 

Congratulations! You have been elected to the 
Longview Chamber of Commerce. 
You are a fine and honorable citizen, and we believe 
you will help strengthen our business community.

Best wishes, 



Harold Potter
President

1213.name: ALM5
1213.text:
Dear 

After 25 years as president of the Chamber of Commerce,
I have finally decided to retire. Congratulations! 
You have been elected to be the new president. 
I am sure you will do a great job.

Good luck, 


Harold Potter
Past President

1214.name: ALM6
1214.text:
Dear 

Congratulations! You have been elected to the 
Longview Town Council. Everyone in town
knows and respects you.

I know that I can depend on you to work to improve the town.

Yours sincerely,



Charles Cane
Mayor

1215.name: ALM7
1215.text:
Dear 

Everyone on the town council supports your decision                                                                                              to run for mayor.  

Before I leave for Kansas City to start my new career 
as a newspaper publisher, I want to offer you my support.
I think you will make a great mayor.

Good luck in July!

Yours sincerely,


Charles Cane
Mayor

1216.name: ALM9
1216.text:
Dear 

Before I leave for Kansas City to start my new career as a 
newspaper publisher, I want to ask you to support Jerry Mander                                                                                           for Mayor in the election this November. Jerry has been very                                                                                            committed to the community for many years.Everyone on the                                                                                               town council thinks he will make a great mayor.However, Jerry                                                                                            is not young, and he probably will not run again in 1920. I suggest                                                                                 that you consider running for mayor at that time.

Yours sincerely,


Charles Cane
Mayor

1217.name: AL14
1217.text:
Dear [FIRSTNAME],

I'm writing this letter while I ride the rails back east.

I'm sorry I never heard back from you last year. I managed to                                                                                 scrape together the money I needed from other friends and                                                                                         relatives. I worked day and night on the Klondike River, and                                                                                     found $2,000 worth of gold. All's well that ends well, as they say.

Please give my regards to the family. Tell them I'm on my way to                                                                            New York.   I want to get in touch with our relatives there. Maybe                                                                                    I can do business with them.

Your cousin George

1218.name: AL15
1218.text:
Dear [FIRSTNAME],

I'm writing this letter while I ride the rails back east.  I was sorry                                                                                I never heard back from you last year. I managed to scrape together                                                              the money I needed from other friends and relatives. I worked day                                                                     and night on the Klondike River, but I didn't find any gold. At least I                                                                     didn't starve or freeze to death. All's well that ends well, as they say.

Please give my regards to the family.  Tell them I'm on my way to                                                                       New York. I want to get in touch with our relatives there. Maybe I can                                                                    do business with them.

Your cousin George

1219.name: AL19
1219.text:
October 14, 1901

Hi, folks! This is your cousin George writing from Buffalo,                                                                                         New York. Last month I visited the Pan-American exposition                                                                                        here. Your eyes would have "lit up" if you had seen the Electric                                                                                      Tower! It's a 375-foot-tall building that shows how electric                                                                                         inventions will make our lives easier someday.

Everyone at the exposition was sad when the president                                                                                              was shot here.  
  
Lately, I've been making plans to travel west again. I'm thinking                                                                                          of going to San Francisco to try out the fishing business.

Fondly yours,

1220.name: AL21
1220.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm sorry that it's taken me so long to write. I've been busy 
working. Thanks to your help, I made it through the off-season. 
Then I worked very hard and saved my money.

In this letter I am returning the $100 that you lent me. You will 
see me by the by the end of the year. I want to come back to 
Longview, where I belong. I will not I will not be a burden to you 
there. I will live and work in town.

Your loving son,

1221.name: AL25
1221.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I have great news! I'm coming back to Kansas.
I've been offered a job at the Juste and Kase law firm. 
Their office is in Longview! I believe you know them.

I look forward to seeing you soon.

Your loving son,



P.S. Next year I will start paying you back for the money 
you spent sending me to college.

1222.name: AL27
1222.text:
Dear Cousin, 

I am writing to tell you that our grandfather Benjamin passed 
away in Chicago last week. He went peacefully, in his sleep.                                                                                       The doctor says he died of natural causes. This isn't surprising.                                                                                     He was very old.

Grandpa left you $150 in his will. I have asked his lawyer to send                                                                                    it to the bank in your town.The money should be waiting for you there.

My son George and I send our love to you and your family.

Yours fondly,

1223.name: AL29
1223.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I have good news for you. We've struck oil! 
We've been pumping for about six months now, and the well is
finally dry. Your share of the profit is $2,500.00. I have sent it directly
to your bank.

Thank you for your help, partner!

Yours,

1224.name: AL30
1224.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I'm afraid I don't have good news. It seems
that we picked a piece of land without any oil underneath it.

I'm sorry about the money you lost. I'm sure you'll make it up soon, 
selling wheat and corn.

Thank you for your help anyway.

Yours,

1225.name: AL31
1225.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I finally have a chance to write and tell you
my good news. We've struck oil! We've been pumping for about six 
months now, and the well is finally dry. My partners and I made a profit
of $12,500 from this well.

I hope next time we can work together.

Yours,

1226.name: AL32
1226.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I'm afraid I don't have good news. 
It seems that I picked a piece of land without any oil underneath it.

It's just as well you didn't invest in this well. If I hear of a better deal,
I'll be sure to let you know.


Yours,

1227.name: AL33
1227.text:
Official Enlistment Notice
according to the Selective Service Act of 1917

son2 lastname

You have been drafted by the United States Army.
You must register at the Longview Post Office,
Buffalo County, Kansas, by June 20, 1917.
 


Recruitment Office

1228.name: AL34
1228.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Our greatest fear has come true. Our sons are going off to fight 
in the war.  I hope they meet their Uncle Son2 over there,
so he can look out for them. 
Billy and Davey are only 19 and 21 years old.

Please let me know if you hear any news from Son2.
I've heard that he's going to a place in France where the most
important battles are being fought.

John sends his love.

Your loving daughter,

1229.name: AL35
1229.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm proud to be the first member of our family to earn 
a college degree.

I have decided to use my education to teach at a new school
for young women in Boston. I hope to help in the struggle 
to win the right for women to vote.
In Boston I'm sure I will meet others involved in this struggle.

I am also happy to tell you that I have saved up enough money 
to pay you back for my first year of college.  I have sent $480.00
to your account at the bank in Longview.

Your loving daughter,

1230.name: AL36
1230.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Please let me know if you hear any news from brother. 
Where is he in France?

I have some news of my own. I am leaving my job at the school. 
I am going to work for the National American 
Woman Suffrage Association (NAWSA).
I will be an assistant to Carrie Chapman Catt, its president.
We will be working hard to make sure that Congress 
passes the 19th Amendment next year. 

Your loving daughter,

1231.name: AL37
1231.text:
Somewhere in France

This is the saddest letter I've ever had to write you. I received a 
letter telling me that my beloved mother, Marilla, your first cousin,                                                                     died of the Spanish influenza.  Everyone I know has lost someone                                                                        in their family to this  terrible disease.  Mother was 76 years old,                                                                          but she had always been healthy and strong. She wanted you to                                                                    remember her that way.

By the way, she left you $300 in her will. I am sending a check for                                                                       that amount with this letter.

Yours,

1232.name: AL38
1232.text:
Somewhere in France

Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm not in Kansas anymore! I can't tell you much except that 
I've learned how to dig a trench faster than I used to plow a                                                                            row of dry Kansas soil. I never have quite enough food to eat 
or time to sleep, but the boys I'm with are the best friends
a fellow could ever want.

Tell all the folks back home that we're going to win this war soon.  
I've been on my own for a few years now, but I could sure use a
good, home-cooked meal now!

Until then, your homesick son,

1233.name: AL39
1233.text:
The United States Army is proud to present the Medal
of Honor to Son2 Lastname for service beyond the call
of duty during  the Battle of Chateau-Thierry in July 1918.

Son2 should present himself at the ceremonies on
July 4 in Longview, Kansas, to receive the medal.

The office of General Pershing

1234.name: AL40
1234.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm thrilled to hear that Son2 was awarded the Medal of Honor.
I wish I had been in Longview for the ceremony.  

I'm still waiting for Billy to come back from France. He wrote                                                                                     that his leg is healing nicely, and there will hardly be a scar. 

Ever since Davey came back, he's been applying to colleges. 
He seems in a big hurry to put the war behind him and get 
on with his life.

Please send our love to everyone.

Your loving daughter,

1235.name: AL41
1235.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Victory is very close. Last spring, Congress passed the
19th Amendment. Now we must wait and see how many 
states vote for it. It looks hopeful. I am having the time 
of my life working at NAWSA for a cause in which I believe.

I have other good news. A lawyer named Frederick Fields has 
helped me a lot in my work. We have become quite good friends 
during the past year. He has asked me to marry him, and I have                                                                  accepted. He is from Colorado, so we will surely come back                                                                                 west for the wedding.

Your loving daughter,

1236.name: AL43
1236.text:
On April 8th, 1885, First last  will have met the 
requirements of the Homestead Act of 1862. 
First last paid twenty dollars to the                                                                                                                                         United States government and settled and farmed                                                                                                             160 acres of land for five years.

The United States government will transfer section 9474
in Buffalo County, Kansas, to First last.
First last will be the legal owner of this property.

Signed and sealed,


Robert Evans
Land Registry Clerk

1237.name: AL50
1237.text:
Dear  
Thank you for joining the Buffalo County Farmers' Alliance.  

Big business is getting rich from the work of poor farmers.
This must stop. We will pressure the federal government to take 
over the railroads and end high shipping prices.

We will be strong if we work together. Thank you for your support.

Yours sincerely,


J.W. Paton
President

1238.name: AL51
1238.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I have wonderful news. I'm getting married! Bob Conway                                                                            moved to this country from Ireland 4 years ago. He works                                                                                at the front desk of the nicest hotel in Boston. We will live                                                                                in a small apartment in the North End. I will continue teaching                                                                     English to immigrants.

In my spare time, I have become involved in the struggle for 
women's suffrage. Bob also believes that women should be                                                                      allowed to vote. Wish me luck!

Your loving daughter,

1239.name: AL52
1239.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Please let me know if you hear any news from broth2. 
Where is he in France?

I got a letter from Bob today. He is still somewhere in France. 
He doesn't  write much, except to say that he's homesick. 
It's very hard for us here without him. I'm teaching seven 
extra students to make ends meet.

Bobby Jr. and little Mary send their love.

Your daughter,

1240.name: AL53
1240.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Bob returned safely from France and sends his love. 
Bobby Jr., Mary, and little Harry are well.

Last spring, Congress passed the 19th Amendment,
which would give women the vote. For the past six months,
I've been doing volunteer work a few hours a week with the 
National American Woman Suffrage Association (NAWSA). 
We're trying to convince people to vote for this amendment.
It looks as though the amendment will be ratified. I'm so excited!

Your daughter,

1241.name: AL54
1241.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I have great news! I'm coming back to Kansas. I've been                                                                                                offered a job at the Juste and Kase law firm. Their office                                                                                                     is in Longview! I believe you know them.

I look forward to seeing you soon.

Your loving son,



P.S. Next year I will start paying you back for the money
you spent sending me to college.

1242.name: AL60
1242.text:
Dear Loyal Supporter,
We hope you are doing well during this difficult time. 
Our grain prices continue to drop while railroad shipping
prices remain high. We are writing to ask you to support the 
People's Party. Last year the Populist candidate for president, 
James B. Weaver, received over one million votes. The Populists 
and the Farmers' Alliance have the same goals. Both
organizations want the government to control the railroads. We
also want the government to print more money. We believe that if
there is more money, then prices will rise.  This means that prices
for farm products will rise too. Thank you for your continued support.
Yours sincerely,


J.W. Paton
President

1243.name: AL62
1243.text:
Dear Cousin,

I have some bad news for you. Our biscuit company has gone 
out of business. We have lost a lot of money in the 
past three years, and we owe too much money to continue.
I have sent a final check to your bank. 

We will be fine. My sons and I have found work in factories 
in the city. When we save up enough money, we will try to 
start another business.

Thank you so much for your help in the past.
Fondly,

1301.name: right1
1301.text: Between 1880 and 1950, farmers in the Great Plains states faced all these natural disasters.

1302.name: right2
1302.text:
The French gave the Statue of Liberty to the Americans in 1886, to celebrate America's 100th birthday. It is a larger copy of a statue that stands on the bank 
of the Seine River in Paris.  
Frederic Auguste Bartholdi created the nine-foot original.  The New York  version is a copper and steel structure created 
by Gustave Eiffel (the builder of the Eiffel Tower). The 152-foot-tall Statue of Liberty stands on Liberty Island in New York harbor.  In her left hand, Liberty holds a book that symbolizes the Declaration of Independence.  In her right hand, she holds the torch of freedom.

1303.name: right3
1303.text: In 1884, Theodore Roosevelt left the New York Legislature and moved to North Dakota to be a farmer.  Unfortunately, the Great Plains were suffering from terrible droughts that killed most of the cattle there.  In 1886, Theodore Roosevelt gave up his farm and returned to his political career in New York.

1304.name: right4
1304.text: In 1889, the U.S. government opened part of the Oklahoma territory to homestead settlement.  Thousands of homesteaders rushed to stake out land for themselves.  This was called "The Oklahoma Land Rush."  This land had originally been promised to Native American tribes who had hoped for their own state.

1305.name: right5
1305.text:
In 1889, the state of Washington joined the United States.  
Named in honor of  George Washington, it is the only state named after a president.

1306.name: right6
1306.text: In 1891, Whitcomb L. Judson invented the zipper when he decided that laces, hooks and eyes, and buttons took too long to fasten and unfasten.  Unfortunately, the zipper that Judson invented often came apart without warning.  In 1912, a Swedish engineer named Widen Sundback improved and patented the zipper, making it a popular fastener for clothing.

1307.name: right7
1307.text: Dr. James Naismith, born in Canada, was a physical education professor at the YMCA college in Springfield, Massachusetts.  He invented the game of basketball in December 1891.  Professional basketball games began in New York City in 1896.

1308.name: right8
1308.text:
Andrew Carnegie (1835-1919) founded the Carnegie Steel Company in 1892.  Carnegie was born in Scotland and came to America in 1848.  He was very poor and earned only $1.20 per week at his first job in America. He became very successful. In 1901, his steel company was bought by J. P. Morgan for $480 million, making Carnegie the richest man in the world.  Morgan combined Carnegie's company with other steel properties 
to create the United States Steel Company, which controlled 65 percent of all U.S. steel manufacturing.

1309.name: right9
1309.text:
President William McKinley was 
shot and killed at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, 
in 1901.  He was the 24th president 
of the United States.  
He was a Republican.

1310.name: right10
1310.text: Wilbur and Orville Wright were the pilots of this plane, the Wright Flyer.  They became interested in flying by watching how flying birds twist their wing tips to balance.  For many years, they built flying machines that could fly without engines.  On December 17, 1903, in North Carolina, they made the first piloted flight in an airplane with a motor.  This flight changed the world.  The flight lasted 12 seconds, and the airplane flew nearly 200 feet.  Only nine days earlier, the New York Times had said that man would not fly for 1,000 years.

1311.name: right11
1311.text:
This Model T was introduced by Henry Ford (1863-1947) in 1908.  
It was the first automobile that was successfully mass-produced for the ordinary citizen.  In 1913, Ford built 1,000 Model T cars each day.

1312.name: right12
1312.text: All these products were available in 1908, but only peanuts and Cracker Jacks were mentioned in the song.

1313.name: right13
1313.text:
There was very little rainfall in the Great Plains states.  A farm of 160 acres could not raise enough crops to support a homestead family.  In addition, ranchers needed bigger grazing areas.  The Homestead Enlargement Act of 1909 doubled the amount of land that Congress had given the farmers in the Homestead Act of 1862.  This was still not enough land for many farmers.  They continued to 
struggle for survival.

1314.name: right14
1314.text: This was the Titanic, a British luxury cruise ship.  In 1912, on its first trip from England to New York, it sank.  Of the 2,224 people on board, 1,513 drowned.  This was the worst sea disaster ever.

1315.name: right15
1315.text:
The Panama Canal was completed in 1914.  It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.  Ships can use the canal to go from one ocean to the other, without traveling around the 
tip of South America.  The canal 
was built by the United States, 
which still owns it.  According to an agreement that was signed in 1978, the country of Panama will take 
over full control of the canal in 1999.

1391.name: triv16
1391.text: Which ray was discovered by Wilhelm Roentgen in 1895?

1396.name: right16
1396.text: Wilhelm C. Roentgen, a German scientist, discovered the X ray in 1895. It is a powerful ray of light that can pass through things that ordinary rays of light cannot enter.  X rays are used to take pictures of parts of the body that cannot be seen from the outside, such as organs and bones.  Roentgen called these rays X rays because he did not completely understand them.
